title: Separated locally quasi-finite geometry of an affine etale relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $U$ be an affine $S$-scheme, meaning a scheme isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a commutative ring $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $R$ be an $S$-scheme and let $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be a monomorphism such that $R(T)$ is an equivalence relation on $U(T)$ for every $S$-scheme $T$. Suppose $s,t:R\to U$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then each of the three morphisms $s$, $t$, and $j$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. No separatedness hypothesis on $S$ and no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $R$ are imposed.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first two paragraphs of the proof (separatedness of R, s, t and j, and local quasi-finiteness of j); local quasi-finiteness of s,t is the unramified consequence used in the first representability step.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-square-monomorphism-absolute-separated] to the given monomorphism $j:R\to U\times_SU$ and an affine presentation of $U$. It gives the absolute separatedness of $R$, without any separatedness hypothesis on $S$. Writing $a_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $a_R:R\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ for structure maps, we have $a_U\circ s=a_R=a_U\circ t$. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation] applied to these factorizations makes both $s$ and $t$ separated.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first proof paragraph; Schemes Tag 01KV, lemma-compose-after-separated

proof.text: By [def-weil-etale-morphism], both $s$ and $t$ are unramified. The definition [def-weil-unramified-morphism] also gives that $s$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] to each projection: both are locally quasi-finite in the pointwise sense of the statement. Thus the projections have both required properties.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, first representability step, citing Morphisms Tag 02V5, lemma-unramified-quasi-finite; Morphisms Tag 02GV, lemma-flat-unramified-etale

proof.text: Put $V=U\times_SU$ and let $\pi_1:V\to U$ be its first projection. By the defining projections of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], $\pi_1\circ j=s$, which is locally of finite type by step 2. Apply [lem-trf-monomorphism-finite-type-composite-lqf] with $f=j$ and $g=\pi_1$. Its monomorphism hypothesis is given, and its composite hypothesis has just been verified. It gives that $j$ is separated and locally quasi-finite in the required pointwise sense. Together with steps 1 and 2 these are all six conclusions; no step uses quasi-compactness of $R$.

source.place: Tag 0265, lemma-presentation-quasi-compact, second proof paragraph; Morphisms Tag 02GE, lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism, and Tag 02V5, lemma-unramified-quasi-finite

lean.statement: theorem affine_etale_relation_separated_locally_quasi_finite {S : Scheme.{u}} (R U : Over S) [IsAffine U.left] (s t : R ⟶ U) [Mono (pullback.lift s.left t.left (s.w.trans t.w.symm))] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Etale s.left] [Etale t.left] : (IsSeparated s.left ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite s.left) ∧ (IsSeparated t.left ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite t.left) ∧ (IsSeparated (pullback.lift s.left t.left (s.w.trans t.w.symm)) ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (pullback.lift s.left t.left (s.w.trans t.w.symm)))
